To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
glial cells express hepatocyte growth factor, which stimulates secretion of vascular endothelial growth factors.
glial cells express HGF in epiretinals membranes of patients with vitreoretinal diseases and that HGF is a mitogenic factor and a stimulator for chemotaxis of glial cells.
glial cells of the retina express HGF and its receptor, c-Met.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of HGF as an autocrine/ paracrine regulator of glial cell proliferation and chemotactic migration, which may have a role in the development of vitreoretinal diseases.
the role of glial cells in vitreoretinopathies.
the expression of Hgf and c-Met in human proliferative vitreorentinal disorders and the effects of Hgf on retinal glial MIO-M1 cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the expression of hepatocyte-growth factor by glial cells in PVR and PDR may contribute to glial cell proliferation and to retinal neovasculogenesis, via the stimulation of the vascular endothelium growth factor.

glial cell expression of HGF is a feature of epiretinal membrane formation, which may contribute to the pathogenesis of proliferative vitreoretiopathy and proliferative diabetic vitreoretinopathies, respectively.
glial cells express and respond to HGF in vitreoretina.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
glial cells may play an important role in the pathogenesis of PDR and PVR by producing HGF and VEGF, which may be responsible for neovascularization and proliferation of the retinal cells.
HGF may be involved in the development of PVR by promoting glial cell proliferation and migration, and by stimulating VEGF release.
glial cells are a source of HGF and c-Met in the human eye, and that glial-derived HGF may contribute to the development of vitreoretinal disease by inducing VEGF secretion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HGF is a potent stimulator of VEGF production in glial cells and that this effect is likely mediated by activation of the PI3K pathway.
the glial cells in the retina are able to secrete HGF and respond to it.
glial cells can express HGF, the ligand for c-Met.
